articles.title: Lyon v Crystal Palace, Torreense v Sunderland, and more: Europa League – live
articles.summary: ⚽ Europa League updates from the 5.45pm BST kick-offs ⚽ Live scoreboard | Read Football Daily | Email Michael. Pierre Sage is something of a Lyon man, a Lyonnais if you will.
body: Our early kick-offs are full of wonder. Torreense might be struggling domestically this season but after becoming the first Portuguese second tier club to lift the Taça de Portugal with a 2-1 win over Sporting in May, they beat Lillestrom in their Europa League opener and are relishing the visit of Sunderland. The Black Cats are also hoping their European adventures kickstart their domestic season, with Régis Le Bris’ side down in 17th in the Premier League having also won their Europa League opener – beating AZ last month.

There is plenty more besides. Both RB Salzburg v Milan and Union Saint-Gilloise v Real Sociedad feel like they could be Champions League fixtures in another campaign, while Bayer Leverkusen face a tricky trip to Lech Poznan.
Here are the 5.45pm BST games we will be covering in this liveblog, while Simon Burnton will be along later with a separate clockwatch to cover the 8pm BST kick-offs. Enjoy!

articles.title: Giovanni Leoni’s return from injury delayed in fresh blow to Liverpool
articles.summary: Defender sustained ACL injury on debut for club. Iraola: ‘It is taking more time than we wanted’ Giovanni Leoni’s Liverpool return has been delayed because of the severity of the knee injury sustained on his debut, Andoni Iraola has revealed.
body: The central defender had been expected to resume team training during the recent international break but that schedule has been put back by about a month.

Leoni, a £26m signing from Parma in 2025, sustained an anterior cruciate ligament injury against Southampton 13 months ago. Iraola has disclosed the damage extended beyond the ACL and Liverpool must tread carefully with the 19-year-old’s rehabilitation as a consequence.

“It is taking more time than we wanted,” the head coach said. “With Gio, the plan was to train with the team in this past international break. It is probably now going to be the next international break [which starts on 9 November], so we have lost one month in the process.

“With Giovanni’s injury, I wasn’t here but talking to the medical department it wasn’t just an ACL. It was a bad injury, a lot of things around the knee were involved apart from the ACL. I think he has to be very confident in the rehab and the process has to be very careful with him.

articles.title: British Cycling to act after 'toxic' survey responses
articles.summary: British Cycling is to launch an "action plan" following a survey in which some responses reportedly described its World Class Programme as "toxic".
body: The confidential survey was funded by UK Sport and carried out by an independent company earlier this year.

The Times reported, external that the results found there was a drop in morale among riders and performance staff, while "toxic" was the joint-second most common response to a question asking for words to describe the programme.
"The wellbeing of our staff and riders is fundamental to everything we do at British Cycling," said a British Cycling spokesperson.
"The Culture Feedback Survey, which has been the subject of recent reports, is independently run to provide a valuable tool to help us learn and improve.

articles.title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ role as Women’s Champions League presenter
articles.summary: Scott walking away to focus on other projects. Disney+ was criticised after opening round this season. Alex Scott, the former Football Focus host, has left her role as a presenter of the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+.
body: It is understood it was Scott’s decision to walk away and focus on other projects, including her new show, One More Word WSL, with her fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.
Scott had fronted the streaming platform’s coverage of the elite women’s European club competition since obtaining the rights in 2025.

Disney’s production levels were criticised after the opening round of fixtures this season after a series of technical problems, including an unscheduled advert break that interrupted the second half of Arsenal’s 1-0 win over HB Køge for more than three minutes.

A spokesperson for Disney+ told the Guardian: “We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women’s Champions League on Disney+. Her passion for the women’s game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success.”

articles.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
articles.summary: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game…
body: Not just because Désiré Doué was unplayable or that Vitinha put on an absolute clinic or that Luis Enrique was more forward-thinking than Magnus Carlsen reading a horoscope in playing his right-back as a striker, but also because the camera kept cutting – deliciously – to the faces of glum City fans as they watched their expensively assembled squad spin into such a dizzy mess that £125m Enzo Fernández and £116m Elliott Anderson appeared in Manchester to be auditioning as a double act for next year’s Strictly.

Although PSG eased off in the second half as City rallied to a brave 4-2 home defeat, it was a miserable outing for all of those dressed in sky blue or trendy flatcaps sitting in the stands. Pep Guardiola was – we think – not one of the City fans that had spent the weekend chanting “we’re Man City, we’ll cheat when we want” at Anfield – but the former manager returned to Manchester for a well-timed visit on Wednesday to support City’s beleaguered owners, backing up last month’s statement that he remains “behind my club”.

articles.title: Walsh vomit & Ponga pain - the physical toll of World Cup opener
articles.summary: Australia's Reece Walsh exerted himself to the point of throwing up, while New Zealand's Kalyn Ponga tried to play on with a suspected broken arm in a dramatic Men's Rugby League World Cup opener.
body: If anyone doubted the physical commitment of rugby league's greatest stars, they only needed to watch an exhausted Reece Walsh doubled up and vomiting during Thursday's epic World Cup opener between Australia and New Zealand.
And during the Kangaroos' dramatic 24-22 victory in Sydney, there were plenty of other examples of that commitment - aside from the normal rough and tumble this punishing sport regularly delivers.

New Zealand full-back Kalyn Ponga bravely battled on for 20 minutes with a suspected broken arm before almost having to be scraped off the pitch minutes before hat-trick hero Jack Bostock's winning try for the Kangaroos.

Mitchell Moses initially tried to run off a calf issue before being forced from the field just after the break, while Australia captain Isaah Yeo demonstrated his durability against a powerhouse Kiwis pack, having elected to delay surgery on his injured pectoral muscle just in order play in the tournament.

articles.title: Warren paints heavyweight unification picture for 2027
articles.summary: Promoter Frank Warren wants to stage heavyweight world-title unification fights in 2027 and hopes to bring former undisputed champion Oleksandr Usyk back into the mix.
body: The division's four major titles are now held by different champions, with Warren promoting three of them, including Daniel Dubois, who defends his WBO belt against Fabio Wardley in London on Saturday.
"The plan is to make the unification fights happen and try to get Usyk back in it," Warren told the 5 Live Boxing podcast.
Dubois and Wardley meet at the O2 Arena, five months after Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to stop his British rival in the 11th round of a thrilling encounter in Manchester.
Warren, who also promotes WBC champion Agit Kabayel and IBF title-holder Filip Hrgovic, believes Saturday's winner will be in a strong position to pursue further world titles.

articles.title: Will Campbell streamlines stages of grief after latest knee injury
articles.summary: Coming out of college, durability was one of Will Campbell’s many strengths. Not even halfway through his second season with the New England Patriots, he has missed time due to injury twice already.
body: The second of those injuries happened against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, and it did leave the 22-year-old not only in pain. It also, by his own admission, left him quite angry at the situation.
“Just mad. That’s really all it was. I was just pissed off,” Campbell told reporters at his Gillette Stadium locker on Wednesday.
For Campbell, hurting his right knee after getting rolled up on from behind is unfortunately nothing new. The same thing happened to him during his 2025 rookie season in a game against the Bengals.

He missed the next four contests as a result of that particular injury before returning for the regular season finale and later New England’s playoff run. However, he was a shell of his former self upon coming back from the torn MCL he had sustained.

articles.title: McKibbin one off lead in Delhi with McIlroy in contention
articles.summary: Tom McKibbin is one shot off the lead and Rory McIlroy three further back after a weather-disrupted opening day of the DP World India Championship.
body: Denmark's Niklas Norgaard topped the leaderboard on day one after a six-under-par round of 66 which included an eagle, six birdies and two bogeys at the Delhi Golf Club.
McKibbin, Spaniard Eugenio Chacarra and Belgian Thomas Detry all reached five under as they completed their opening rounds.

Play was suspended because of lightning and torrential rain shortly after 06:30 BST, and did not resume until five hours later, leaving many of the field unable to finish their first 18 holes and preventing others from starting their rounds.
McKibbin posted six birdies, with his card marred by a solitary bogey, to put himself well in contention.

articles.title: Greg Olsen linked to Jim Nantz, CBS amid uncertain Fox future
articles.summary: The sports media landscape could see significant change heading into the 2027 NFL season. Earlier this season CBS announced its plans to move on from Tony Romo, choosing instead to roll with former NFL star J.J. Watt alongside play-by-play man Jim Nantz.
body: The “Thursday Night Football” broadcast booth could also be in flux as Al Michaels sits in the final year of his contract. Prime Video recently signed Kirk Herbstreit to a new deal, but one that includes a potential out if someone like Rams head coach Sean McVay becomes available.

And then there’s Greg Olsen. The beloved color analyst who received critical acclaim for his broadcasts was swiftly demoted by Fox, which inked a lucrative deal with former NFL star quarterback Tom Brady.
Media insider Richard Deitsch revealed Olsen is in the final year of his contract with Fox and the two sides haven’t discussed a new deal.
The insider then linked Olsen to the CBS job after the two sides “had exploratory talks” two years ago and suggested he would be a “very attractive free agent” on the open media market.

With the final European Tour event of 2026 taking place at MECC Maastricht from October 16-18, the race for European Championship qualification reaches its climax on Dutch soil, with 'The Green Machine' determined to end his title drought in front of his home crowd.
Van Gerwen's last big tournament success came at the Nordic Darts Masters in June, where he defeated Luke Humphries in the final.
His last major TV title before that came on home soil at the 2025 World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

articles.title: Browns WR Jerry Jeudy ‘fits the bill’ as a trade target for a top team
articles.summary: The NFL trade deadline is not until November 10th this year, leaving a lot of time and games on the schedule for rumors to come and go. Some rumors will occur, like QB Shedeur Sanders yesterday, for oddly specific reasons.
body: Given how well rookie WRs KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston have looked and played, Jeudy’s future in Cleveland seems tenuous at best. The veteran has been a good influence on the younger players but only has one more year on his contract and isn’t being used regularly by the Browns.

If Kansas City can send a Day 3 pick for the 27-year-old wideout, it could be a strong option to replenish the Chiefs’ playmaking for this season and the future without taking a huge risk. He is signed through the 2027 season, with a $13.4 million cap hit next year.

Arrowhead Pride noted that former Cleveland wide receiver coach Chad O’Shea is now in the same role in Kansas City. That familiarity could help not only lead to a trade, but help Jeudy get adjusted to a new offense quickly.

The Browns and Chiefs are familiar with working deals together, as the two teams combined on a deal near the top of the 2026 NFL draft, allowing Kansas City to move up a few spots to select CB Mansoor Delane.

articles.title: McIlroy four off lead on delayed first day in India
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy shot a two-under par opening round to finish four shots behind the clubhouse lead on a part-suspended first day of play at the DP World India Championship in New Delhi.
body: McIlroy was midway through the back nine when play was stopped for thunder and lightning in the area, with players then off the course for over four hours.
When play did resume at 4pm local time, McIlroy completed a round of 70 to sit tied 13th.
The world No 2 started from the par-four 10th, which he bogeyed, and went out in 34 after birdies at the 13th, 15th and 18th.
He found another birdie at the second hole but followed that with a second bogey of the round at the third, before finishing with six successive pars.
